constrained-v2.decoding: pinyin-constrained beam (width 4, per-path KV history, fuzzy pairs an/ang en/eng in/ing z/zh c/ch s/sh at syllable level), invariant seed context '。', no prompt, no chat template
constrained-v2.confidence_semantics: geometric mean of raw (not mask-renormalized) next-token softmax probabilities; small absolute values that decay with length — comparable only within this route, never against prompt-route confidences

history_note: An earlier constrained-v1 measurement (89.9% accuracy, p50 151ms) was taken with two decoder defects: beam paths scored against wrong KV histories, and final-swap fuzzy matching only applied to bare syllables. Both are fixed in constrained-v2; the v2 numbers above are the designed system. Latency doubled as the price of per-path histories — cross-path KV sharing (prefix-tree cache) is the known optimization path.
conclusion: Constrained decoding beats the prompt route decisively at the same model size: 92.2% vs 72.6% sentence accuracy. The prompt route is effectively non-functional on 0.5B for this dataset (910/974 empty suggestions; its accuracy equals the dictionary fallback). The constrained decoder never returns illegal text (mask + worker fuzzy gate); the eval-side exact-pinyin gate still rejects 19 of its outputs, which are precisely fuzzy corrections the harness's stricter matching does not credit. Latency parity is lost: the prompt route prefills once per request while the constrained route re-prefills per diverging beam path (p50 281ms vs 158ms on MPS fp16) — KV-prefix sharing is the next lever.
